title: Sales by Day of the Week

sections.Description:
You are given two tables:

**Orders**: `(order_id int, customer_id int, order_date date, item_id varchar, quantity int)`. `(order_id, item_id)` is the primary key. Each row says the customer ordered `quantity` units of `item_id` on `order_date`.

**Items**: `(item_id varchar, item_name varchar, item_category varchar)`. `item_id` is the primary key.

As the business owner you want a sales report by item category and day of the week. Write a query that reports **how many units in each category have been ordered on each day of the week**. The result has one row per category with columns `Category`, `Monday`, `Tuesday`, `Wednesday`, `Thursday`, `Friday`, `Saturday`, `Sunday`. Categories with no orders still appear (with 0s). Return the result ordered by category.
sections.Examples:
**Example 1:**  
Input:  
Orders:

| order_id | customer_id | order_date | item_id | quantity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 2020-06-01 | 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 1 | 2020-06-08 | 2 | 10 |
| 3 | 2 | 2020-06-02 | 1 | 5 |
| 4 | 3 | 2020-06-03 | 3 | 5 |
| 5 | 4 | 2020-06-04 | 4 | 1 |
| 6 | 4 | 2020-06-05 | 5 | 5 |
| 7 | 5 | 2020-06-05 | 1 | 10 |
| 8 | 5 | 2020-06-14 | 4 | 5 |
| 9 | 5 | 2020-06-21 | 3 | 5 |

Items:

| item_id | item_name | item_category |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | LC Alg. Book | Book |
| 2 | LC DB. Book | Book |
| 3 | LC SmarthPhone | Phone |
| 4 | LC Phone 2020 | Phone |
| 5 | LC SmartGlass | Glasses |
| 6 | LC T-Shirt XL | T-Shirt |

Output:

| Category | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday | Saturday | Sunday |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Book | 20 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| Glasses | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| Phone | 0 | 0 | 5 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 10 |
| T-Shirt | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

*Explanation: On Monday (2020-06-01 and 2020-06-08) 10 + 10 = 20 units of Book (items 1, 2) were sold. On Tuesday (2020-06-02) 5 Book units. On Wednesday (2020-06-03) 5 Phone units. On Thursday (2020-06-04) 1 Phone unit. On Friday (2020-06-05) 10 Book units and 5 Glasses units. Nothing was sold on Saturday. On Sunday (2020-06-14 and 2020-06-21) 5 + 5 = 10 Phone units. T-Shirt has no sales, yet still appears with zeros.*
sections.Thought Process (as if you’re the interv:
The output is a **pivot**: one row per category and one column per weekday. Start from Items (so categories without orders are kept) and LEFT JOIN Orders on `item_id`. Group by `item_category`, and for each weekday use conditional aggregation: `SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(order_date) = k THEN quantity ELSE 0 END)`.

In MySQL, `DAYOFWEEK` returns 1 for Sunday, 2 for Monday, ... 7 for Saturday (alternatively compare `DAYNAME(order_date)` with the weekday name). A category with no orders has a NULL `order_date`, so every CASE falls to ELSE 0 and the sums are 0. Finally order by category.
sections.Corner cases to consider:
- Category with no orders at all (needs the LEFT JOIN from Items; all zeros)
- Weekday with no sales (0, not NULL)
- Several items in one category and several orders on one day (summed)
- Sunday is the last column even though MySQL numbers it as 1
- Items that were never ordered but share a category with ordered items
sections.Solution:
```sql
SELECT
    i.item_category AS Category,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(o.order_date) = 2 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Monday,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(o.order_date) = 3 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Tuesday,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(o.order_date) = 4 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Wednesday,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(o.order_date) = 5 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Thursday,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(o.order_date) = 6 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Friday,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(o.order_date) = 7 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Saturday,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(o.order_date) = 1 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Sunday
FROM Items i
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON i.item_id = o.item_id
GROUP BY i.item_category
ORDER BY i.item_category;
```
sections.Time and Space complexity Analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** O(I + O) to join and scan items and orders (with an index on `Orders(item_id)`), plus sorting the C categories.
- **Space Complexity:** O(C), one aggregated row per category (7 sums each).
sections.Potential follow-up questions (as if you:
- How would you report revenue instead of units?  
  *Hint: Join a price column and sum `quantity * price` in each CASE.*
- How do you keep the weekday columns in Monday-Sunday order?  
  *Hint: The column order is fixed by the SELECT list, so it never depends on DAYOFWEEK's numbering.*
- What if the weekday set were dynamic (e.g. by month)?  
  *Hint: Use dynamic SQL / a pivot, or return long format (category, day, total).*
sections.Summary: This is the **conditional-aggregation pivot** pattern: group by one dimension (category), and spread a second dimension (weekday) into columns with `SUM(CASE WHEN ...)`. Starting from the dimension table with a LEFT JOIN ensures empty categories still show up.
sections.Flashcard: LEFT JOIN Items to Orders, GROUP BY item_category, and pivot weekdays with SUM(CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(order_date) = k THEN quantity ELSE 0 END); order by category.
